symptom: After upgrading mxcli (nightly-174 -> nightly-20261113), create or modify microflow of three flows mxcli itself wrote from unchanged scripts with no @position was refused with MDL-V1-REBUILD: an if without else in a call's error handler ('changes where its paths end or meet'), a falling-through handler inside nested guards ('the stored statement "Join" has no activity to address'), a nested while whose body holds an if around an unnamed create ('changes inside its body').
cause: builtAsStored paired built and stored objects by position. Commit 5e9c54c2 (ako/mxcli#1773, a correct layout-measurer fix) moved where the builder draws unpositioned nodes, so a flow stored by the previous release no longer paired, and the body fell through to the statement diff, which does not match these describe shapes (empty else inside a handler — canonicalFlow never entered handler bodies; the join/merge chain of a rejoining handler; describe's `$Var = create` for an unnamed create inside a loop body).
fix: When the position pairing differs, builtAsStored compares once more with objects paired by the flows between them (from the start, outgoing flows ordered by error-handler flag and case) and sets aside Position/Size/RelativeMiddle of objects at no stated point, and connection indices when the script states no anchor. canonicalFlow now also canonicalises (and counts joins in) error-handler bodies, so the empty else there matches when the flow does change elsewhere.
insight: 'The builder is deterministic, so an identical re-run matches by construction' holds within one release only: any layout change breaks every unpositioned mxcli-written flow at once, and the statement diff's shape gaps become user-visible. Bisect with the reporter's pre-rebaseline units (git archive a1907ba^) and exec, not check (older checks did not predict exec refusals); a debug print of sameBuiltFlow's why ('nothing stored at …@1185,200' vs stored 1160,200) pinned it in one run. To reproduce without the old release, move the stored nodes (UpdateMicroflow) and re-run the script.
